title: What We’ve Learned About the Coronavirus

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《Dealbook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的Dealbook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领导者，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯汀·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 届时，你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日通过nytimes.com进行部分采访的直播，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: November 18th.
If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Donald, the pandemic feels different in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德，疫情在美国的感觉似乎与

sentences.en: than it did two weeks ago, three weeks ago, a month ago.
sentences.zh: 两周前、三周前、一个月前有所不同。

sentences.en: It feels, and these are highly qualitative words, and I know you're probably rolling your eyes.
sentences.zh: 这种感觉——这些是非常定性的词汇，我知道你可能在翻白眼——

sentences.en: It feels less desperate, and it feels a little less urgent, and I'm not even quite sure why that is.
sentences.zh: 感觉没那么绝望，也没那么紧迫了，我甚至不太确定为什么会这样。

sentences.en: So what do you make of that?
sentences.zh: 那么你是怎么看的呢？

sentences.en: I mean, does that mean we've gotten
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是否意味着我们已经

sentences.en: complacent?
sentences.zh: 变得自满了？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think some parts of the country are not afraid yet.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个国家的一些地区还不感到害怕。

sentences.en: They see this as something that happened to the other, to urban New Yorkers, to Blacks and Hispanics in the big cities far away.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这只是发生在别人身上的事，是发生在遥远大城市里的纽约人、黑人和拉美裔身上的事。

sentences.en: But I also see that even in New York, it's a combination of, well, we survived the first wave, and it didn't get me or
sentences.zh: 但我也看到，即使在纽约，这也是一种综合因素，好吧，我们熬过了第一波疫情，它没有找上我，或者

sentences.en: the people I knew who got it survived.
sentences.zh: 我认识的那些感染者也都挺过来了。

sentences.en: And boy, am I bored and frustrated and locked down, and I want my job back, and I want my hanging out with my friends back.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我感到厌烦、沮丧，被困在家里，我想要回我的工作，想要回到和朋友们在一起的日子。

sentences.en: And I think we have gotten used to the idea of death, of absorbing a lot of death.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我们已经习惯了死亡的概念，习惯了承受大量的死亡。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague, Donald
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事唐纳德·G·

sentences.en: G.
sentences.zh: 麦克尼尔二世，将带来关于新冠病毒现状的最新报道，以及我们在疫情爆发六个月后对该病毒的了解。

sentences.en: McNeil Jr., returns with an update on the state of the coronavirus and what we've learned about the virus six months into the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月15日，星期一。

sentences.en: It's Monday, June 15th.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月15日。

sentences.en: Donald, the last time that we spoke to you was in mid-April, when the death toll from the coronavirus in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德，我们上次和你交谈是在4月中旬，当时美国的新冠病毒死亡人数

sentences.en: was nearing 40,000.
sentences.zh: 接近4万人。

sentences.en: And various states at that time were beginning the process of opening back up, slowly, but opening back up.
sentences.zh: 当时各个州正开始缓慢地重新开放，虽然缓慢，但确实在重新开放。

sentences.en: Where is the pandemic now?
sentences.zh: 现在的疫情情况如何？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, there are 113,000 dead in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 嗯，据我上次查看，美国已有11.3万人死亡。

sentences.en: the last time I looked.
sentences.zh: 据我上次查看。

sentences.en: Basically, every state has reopened to some extent in different ways, with different phases.
sentences.zh: 基本上，每个州都以不同的方式、不同的阶段在某种程度上重新开放了。

sentences.en: In about 21 of those states, cases are going up, as was feared.
sentences.zh: 在大约21个州，病例正如人们所担心的那样在上升。

sentences.en: Hospitalizations are going up.
sentences.zh: 住院人数也在增加。

sentences.en: So I would see this as a very worrying situation.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是一个非常令人担忧的情况。

sentences.en: Well, given that, I mean, in terms of how the United States is managing the virus and its spread, are we doing better now than we were many, many weeks ago when we spoke?
sentences.zh: 那么，考虑到这一点，我的意思是，就美国如何管理病毒及其传播而言，我们现在是否比几周前我们交谈时做得更好？

sentences.en: Are we doing worse?
sentences.zh: 还是做得更差了？

sentences.en: I think we're doing considerably worse in that now we know what the danger is, and yet we're still getting enormous number of infections.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们做得相当糟糕，因为现在我们已经知道危险所在，却仍然有大量的感染病例。

sentences.en: Now, the places that were hit hard in the first wave, which is New York and the Northeast, but also places far away from that, like New Orleans,
sentences.zh: 现在，第一波疫情中受灾严重的地区，即纽约和东北部，以及远离那里的地方，比如新奥尔良、

sentences.en: Seattle, and California, they are mostly coming down.
sentences.zh: 西雅图和加利福尼亚，病例大多在下降。

sentences.en: They got seriously scared.
sentences.zh: 他们真的被吓到了。

sentences.en: They had intense lockdowns that lasted relatively long.
sentences.zh: 他们进行了相对较长时间的严格封锁。

sentences.en: They are wearing masks.
sentences.zh: 他们正在佩戴口罩。

sentences.en: They are practicing social distancing, and cases are coming down in those states.
sentences.zh: 他们正在进行社交疏离，这些州的病例正在下降。

sentences.en: In states where there wasn't a big first wave of the virus, where they were more upset by the economic effects of the lockdown, lots of people out of
sentences.zh: 在那些没有经历过第一波大流行、对封锁带来的经济影响感到更不满的州，很多人失业，

sentences.en: work, lots of people suffering, lots of people frustrated in their houses.
sentences.zh: 很多人受苦，很多人在家里感到沮丧。

sentences.en: Those are where the cases in general are going up.
sentences.zh: 这些地方的病例总体上在上升。

sentences.en: Places like Texas, places like North and South Carolina, places like
sentences.zh: 像德克萨斯州、北卡罗来纳州和南卡罗来纳州，以及

sentences.en: Arizona.
sentences.zh: 亚利桑那州这样的地方。

sentences.en: And that's dangerous because they're coming out of lockdown and opening society and
sentences.zh: 这很危险，因为他们在病例已经处于上升趋势时，解除了封锁，开放了社会，

sentences.en: encouraging people to be in greater contact with each other at a time when the cases are already on the upswing.
sentences.zh: 并鼓励人们加强彼此之间的接触。

sentences.en: So you're not flattening the curve.
sentences.zh: 所以你们并没有拉平曲线。

sentences.en: You're allowing the curve to spike up again.
sentences.zh: 你们是在让曲线再次飙升。

sentences.en: So is it fair to say at this point in the pandemic, the cities and the states that were hardest hit at the
sentences.zh: 那么，在疫情的这个阶段，是否可以公平地说，在疫情初期受灾最严重的城市和州，

sentences.en: beginning seem to have enforced the strongest lockdowns, and therefore the virus infection rates
sentences.zh: 似乎实施了最严格的封锁，因此那里的病毒感染率

sentences.en: seem to be going down there, whereas states that weren't hit as hard at the beginning and perhaps didn't respond as forcefully are now experiencing an uptick in infections instead?
sentences.zh: 似乎正在下降，而那些在初期受灾没那么严重、或许应对也没那么有力的州，现在反而出现了感染激增的情况？

sentences.en: Yes, in general, that's correct.
sentences.zh: 是的，总的来说是这样。

sentences.en: So Donald, now that we have lived with this virus for about half a year, I want to turn
sentences.zh: 那么唐纳德，既然我们已经与这种病毒共存了大约半年，我想转而谈谈

sentences.en: to the things that we have learned about it and that we didn't know when we first started talking to you.
sentences.zh: 我们对它了解到的、而在我们刚开始和你交谈时所不知道的事情。

sentences.en: And I wonder if we can start with transmission.
sentences.zh: 我想我们可以从传播方式开始谈起。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I remember you telling me back in February, the main modes of transmission are droplets.
sentences.zh: 我记得你在二月份告诉我，主要的传播方式是飞沫。

sentences.en: You cough or sneeze near me, I catch the virus from you.
sentences.zh: 你在我附近咳嗽或打喷嚏，我就从你那里感染了病毒。

sentences.en: The other was the virus living on surfaces.
sentences.zh: 另一种是病毒在物体表面存活。

sentences.en: And I would touch that surface, I might touch my eye, I would get infected.
sentences.zh: 我可能会触摸那个表面，然后触摸我的眼睛，从而被感染。

sentences.en: What have we learned about the actual levels of transmission from these two?
sentences.zh: 我们对这两种方式的实际传播水平了解到了什么？

sentences.en: Did one of them turn out to be a much bigger vector than the other?
sentences.zh: 其中一种是否被证明是比另一种更大的传播媒介？

sentences.en: Those two are still vectors, although surfaces may be a little less important than we feared.
sentences.zh: 这两种仍然是传播媒介，尽管物体表面的重要性可能比我们担心的要小一些。

sentences.en: But the really important thing we've learned is that there is aerosol transmission, little tiny, tiny droplets, the kind that hang in the
sentences.zh: 但我们学到的真正重要的事情是存在气溶胶传播，即那些微小的、细小的飞沫，那种可以在

sentences.en: air inside a room for hours, can hold enough virus to transmit this disease.
sentences.zh: 室内空气中悬浮数小时的飞沫，足以携带足够的病毒来传播这种疾病。

sentences.en: And we emit those droplets not just through coughing or sneezing, but just through talking, especially loud talking, through laughing, through singing.
sentences.zh: 我们排放这些飞沫不仅是通过咳嗽或打喷嚏，仅仅通过说话，尤其是大声说话、大笑、唱歌都会排放。

sentences.en: You know, we're unaware of this fine mist of droplets that comes out of our mouth at all times.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们并没有意识到这种时刻从我们嘴里喷出的细微飞沫雾。

sentences.en: You're only sort of aware of it if you're in the front row at a theater and you realize the actors are sort of spitting on you.
sentences.zh: 你只有在剧院前排时才会意识到这一点，你会发现演员们好像在向你喷口水。

sentences.en: But actually, if you and I were to sit three or four feet apart and we're talking and joking and laughing, we would actually be spreading
sentences.zh: 但实际上，如果你和我坐在一起，相隔三四英尺，我们一边说话、开玩笑、大笑，我们实际上就在向对方传播

sentences.en: a cloud of a very fine mist of droplets at each other.
sentences.zh: 一团非常细微的飞沫雾。

sentences.en: So we're learning that transmission, particularly in indoor spaces where there is no wind, is probably a major spreader of this because everybody's vulnerable to it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们了解到，传播，特别是在没有风的室内空间，可能是这种病毒的主要传播方式，因为每个人都容易受到感染。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So staying on this idea of what we've learned,
sentences.zh: 那么继续谈谈我们学到了什么这个话题，

sentences.en: asymptomatic carriers, what have we learned about people who may not even know they have the virus?
sentences.zh: 无症状携带者，我们对那些甚至可能不知道自己携带病毒的人了解到了什么？

sentences.en: They don't show any symptoms, but they may be spreading it.
sentences.zh: 他们没有任何症状，但他们可能正在传播病毒。

sentences.en: How much has our understanding changed about how important asymptomatic carriers are in this pandemic?
sentences.zh: 我们对无症状携带者在这场疫情中的重要性的理解发生了多大的变化？

sentences.en: It has changed a lot.
sentences.zh: 发生了很大的变化。

sentences.en: The initial estimates out of China were that there were very few asymptomatic carriers, like 1%.
sentences.zh: 最初来自中国的估计是无症状携带者很少，大约只有1%。

sentences.en: That has turned out to probably be quite wrong.
sentences.zh: 事实证明这很可能是相当错误的。

sentences.en: The CDC estimates that the number of asymptomatic carriers is about one third.
sentences.zh: 美国疾控中心估计无症状携带者的比例约为三分之一。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that changes a lot about how we handle this disease.
sentences.zh: 这改变了我们处理这种疾病的很多方式。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, okay.
sentences.zh: 嗯，好吧。

sentences.en: So temperature checks probably aren't very useful because one of the symptoms you feel is fever.
sentences.zh: 所以体温检查可能没什么用，因为你感觉到的症状之一是发烧。

sentences.en: If you don't feel fever, you can still spread the disease.
sentences.zh: 如果你不觉得发烧，你仍然可以传播这种疾病。

sentences.en: So you're going to have to detect the disease through testing rather than through saying, hey, we got a lot of sick people
sentences.zh: 所以你必须通过检测来发现疾病，而不是通过说，嘿，我们这里有很多生病的人，

sentences.en: around here because one third of your people are not going to be sick, but they're still spreading the disease.
sentences.zh: 因为你三分之一的人不会生病，但他们仍在传播疾病。

sentences.en: So if you wanted to open up your office, you know, to people, like I said, fever checks wouldn't work.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想向人们开放办公室，就像我说的，体温检查是行不通的。

sentences.en: You'd actually have to test everybody.
sentences.zh: 你实际上必须检测每一个人。

sentences.en: You'd have to test them frequently and you'd have to be able to get the results back very quickly because you don't want somebody who's
sentences.zh: 你必须经常检测他们，而且必须能够非常快地得到结果，因为你不想让一个

sentences.en: asymptomatic working in the office for two or three days while you're waiting for the results of the test to come back.
sentences.zh: 无症状的人在办公室工作两三天，而你还在等待检测结果。

sentences.en: And how possible is that kind of testing?
sentences.zh: 那种检测的可能性有多大？

sentences.en: I mean, what you're proposing is every workplace having some sort of mandatory testing system to weed out people who may have the virus
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你提议的是每个工作场所都有某种强制性的检测系统，以剔除可能携带病毒的人，

sentences.en: and especially those who may be asymptomatically infected.
sentences.zh: 尤其是那些可能无症状感染的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's, I mean, there's a lot of thinking about testing.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，关于检测有很多想法。

sentences.en: In the beginning of the, when we only had, you know, 10,000, 20,000 tests, we were only testing people who were sick, who had symptoMs. It was very hard to get a teSt.
sentences.zh: 在疫情初期，当我们只有1万或2万个检测名额时，我们只检测那些生病、有症状的人。很难获得检测机会。

sentences.en: Now we've reached the point where we're on track to get to a million a day, I think.
sentences.zh: 现在我们已经达到了每天一百万次的水平，我想。

sentences.en: When you reach that level, you can use testing for surveillance.
sentences.zh: 当你达到那个水平时，你可以利用检测进行监测。

sentences.en: That is, you sort of look around the country and say, where do we have hotspots?
sentences.zh: 也就是说，你环顾全国，看看哪里有热点地区。

sentences.en: Now, probably to do that right, we need like 5 million tests a day.
sentences.zh: 现在，要正确做到这一点，我们可能需要每天500万次检测。

sentences.en: That's what a Harvard study suggested.
sentences.zh: 这就是哈佛大学的一项研究所建议的。

sentences.en: And it means testing in New York City, but also testing in Winnemucca, Nevada and every place else.
sentences.zh: 这意味着不仅要在纽约市进行检测，还要在内华达州的温尼马卡以及其他任何地方进行检测。

sentences.en: Because you want to know wherever the virus is popping up, you want to spot it.
sentences.zh: 因为你想知道病毒在哪里出现，你想发现它。

sentences.en: And you want to test not just the sick, but a broad spectrum of people.
sentences.zh: 而且你不仅要检测病人，还要检测广泛的人群。

sentences.en: You know, maybe one day you test all the third graders in the county or something like that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许有一天你检测县里所有的三年级学生，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And another day you test everybody in nursing homes and things like that.
sentences.zh: 另一天你检测养老院里的所有人，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Now that's at the 5 million test level.
sentences.zh: 现在这是在500万次检测的水平上。

sentences.en: If you go up, there was a Nobel Prize winning economist at NYU who proposed that if we had
sentences.zh: 如果你再往上，纽约大学有一位诺贝尔奖经济学家提出，如果我们有

sentences.en: 30 million tests a day, we could literally use this as a way to completely reopen the economy.
sentences.zh: 每天3000万次检测，我们完全可以利用这一点来彻底重启经济。

sentences.en: And that would mean everybody who's in contact with other people in an office would have to be tested every day and we'd need rapid results.
sentences.zh: 这意味着办公室里所有与他人接触的人都必须每天接受检测，而且我们需要快速的结果。

sentences.en: And it would cost, he figured, about one and a half billion dollars per week.
sentences.zh: 他计算过，这每周大约需要花费15亿美元。

sentences.en: But he said, you know what?
sentences.zh: 但他说了，你知道吗？

sentences.en: That's a whole lot less than lockdown has been costing us.
sentences.zh: 这比封锁所付出的代价要少得多。

sentences.en: We could completely reopen the economy if we could test 30 million people a day.
sentences.zh: 如果我们每天能检测3000万人，我们就能彻底重启经济。

sentences.en: And we'd save money by having the whole economy go again.
sentences.zh: 而且通过让整个经济重新运转，我们还能省钱。

sentences.en: Now, the logistics of doing that is wildly unimaginable.
sentences.zh: 现在，实现这一目标的后勤工作是极其难以想象的。

sentences.en: The proposal from the NYU economist has been put in the crazy ideas box for now.
sentences.zh: 纽约大学经济学家的提议目前已被放入疯狂想法的盒子里。

sentences.en: And yet people who really study this stuff think of it as, wow, crazy, but good.
sentences.zh: 然而，真正研究这些东西的人认为它很棒，虽然疯狂，但很好。

sentences.en: So what are you going to do?
sentences.zh: 那你打算怎么做？

sentences.en: You know, it depends on what people are willing to commit money to do.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这取决于人们愿意投入多少资金去做。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And for those who have had the virus and have recovered, of which there are hundreds of thousands of people, what are we learning about immunity?
sentences.zh: 对于那些已经感染并康复的人，其中有成千上万的人，我们对免疫力了解到了什么？

sentences.en: We know that people have antibodies.
sentences.zh: 我们知道人们有抗体。

sentences.en: We know they have IgG antibodies, which are the ones that appear later and usually indicate immunity.
sentences.zh: 我们知道他们有IgG抗体，这是后来出现的，通常表明免疫力。

sentences.en: So we know that people turn up positive on antibody tests.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道人们的抗体检测呈阳性。

sentences.en: And, you know, top experts are saying, we think we can assume they're immune to the disease, but we're not sure yet because we don't
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，顶级专家说，我们认为可以假设他们对这种疾病有免疫力，但我们还不确定，因为我们

sentences.en: really know what level of antibodies you need in order to be immune.
sentences.zh: 并不真正知道你需要什么水平的抗体才能免疫。

sentences.en: So nobody's saying, okay, that's it.
sentences.zh: 所以没有人说，好吧，就是这样。

sentences.en: You've passed one teSt. You're immune.
sentences.zh: 你通过了一项测试。你有免疫力了。

sentences.en: That's what people would like to think.
sentences.zh: 那是人们希望认为的。

sentences.en: I know all sorts of people ask me, should I get an antibody test?
sentences.zh: 我知道各种各样的人问我，我应该做抗体检测吗？

sentences.en: And I keep saying, sure, if it's going to make you feel better, get an antibody test, but don't assume you're immune just because you've got a positive.
sentences.zh: 我一直说，当然，如果这能让你感觉好点，就去做抗体检测，但不要仅仅因为检测呈阳性就认为你有免疫力。

sentences.en: You probably are, but we don't know that yet.
sentences.zh: 你可能确实有，但我们还不知道。

sentences.en: It's still too early.
sentences.zh: 现在还为时过早。

sentences.en: So recalling our very last conversation, which we talked about the idea that there might be kind of two
sentences.zh: 回想我们上一次的谈话，我们讨论过可能存在两种想法。

sentences.en: classes of people in this pandemic, the immune and the susceptible, we are not yet at a place of our
sentences.zh: 在这场大流行中，人们分为两类：免疫者和易感者，我们尚未达到

sentences.en: understanding of the coronavirus where anyone is truly considered immune and therefore sort of invulnerable and able to wander the world differently than the rest of us.
sentences.zh: 对冠状病毒的认知程度，即任何人都能被真正视为免疫，从而在某种程度上刀枪不入，能够以不同于我们其他人的方式在世界上游走。

sentences.en: Scientifically speaking, no, we're not there yet.
sentences.zh: 从科学上讲，不，我们还没到那一步。

sentences.en: But practically speaking, a lot of people, even doctors I know who've been infected and have recovered, are behaving as if they're immune.
sentences.zh: 但从实际情况来看，很多人，甚至包括我认识的那些已经感染并康复的医生，表现得好像他们已经免疫了一样。

sentences.en: They're reasonably confident that they're immune.
sentences.zh: 他们相当自信自己已经免疫了。

sentences.en: I mean, they shouldn't let down their guard,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们不应该放松警惕，

sentences.en: A, because it's not smart, and B, because that's a bad example, but they probably worry a whole lot less than they did before.
sentences.zh: 第一，因为这不聪明；第二，因为这会树立一个坏榜样，但他们可能确实比以前担心得少多了。

sentences.en: Now, we do not know how long immunity lasts, and that's going to be another great big question.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们不知道免疫力能持续多久，这将是另一个巨大的问题。

sentences.en: And we can't know that until some months or years have passed because this virus has only been around since November.
sentences.zh: 而且在几个月或几年过去之前，我们无法知道这一点，因为这种病毒从十一月才开始出现。

sentences.en: So probably the immunity is going to last a few years, but we don't know that yet either.
sentences.zh: 所以免疫力可能会持续几年，但我们现在还不知道。

sentences.en: These are all unknowns.
sentences.zh: 这些都是未知数。

sentences.en: Immunology is complicated.
sentences.zh: 免疫学很复杂。

sentences.en: And given everything you just said, under the current circumstances, where will the United States be by the fall when it comes to death?
sentences.zh: 鉴于你刚才所说的一切，在当前情况下，到秋天时，美国的死亡人数会达到什么程度？

sentences.en: I'm very worried about the fall for several reasons, which I can go into if you want to.
sentences.zh: 我非常担心秋天的情况，原因有几个，如果你想听，我可以详细说说。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: We know the virus transmits indoors, and when it gets cold, people aren't going to be able to eat outdoors again.
sentences.zh: 我们知道病毒在室内传播，当天气变冷时，人们将无法再次在户外用餐。

sentences.en: They're going to want to get into warm spaces.
sentences.zh: 他们会想要进入温暖的空间。

sentences.en: So the possibility for transmission is really high.
sentences.zh: 所以传播的可能性真的很高。

sentences.en: We also know, not just from 1918, but from Michael Osterholm at Minnesota has looked at eight influenza epidemics since, I think it's 1763.
sentences.zh: 我们还知道，不仅从1918年的情况来看，明尼苏达大学的迈克尔·奥斯特霍尔姆（Michael Osterholm）研究了自1763年以来的八次流感大流行。

sentences.en: And in each one of them, no matter what time of year the virus first hit, winter, spring, summer, or fall, it faded and then came back several months later
sentences.zh: 在每一次大流行中，无论病毒最初是在一年中的什么时候爆发——冬季、春季、夏季还是秋季——它都会减弱，然后在几个月后卷土重来，

sentences.en: in a much more lethal wave.
sentences.zh: 并带来更致命的浪潮。

sentences.en: And that was the phenomenon in 1918.
sentences.zh: 这就是1918年发生的情况。

sentences.en: There was a brief but scary breakout in Haskell County, Kansas, in army camps and stuff.
sentences.zh: 当时在堪萨斯州哈斯克尔县的军营等地出现了一次短暂但可怕的爆发。

sentences.en: And then the disease mostly disappeared from the United States, seems to have mostly gone overseas and hit the troops in the trenches in
sentences.zh: 然后这种疾病基本上从美国消失了，似乎大部分转移到了海外，袭击了在欧洲战壕里的军队。

sentences.en: Europe.
sentences.zh: 欧洲。

sentences.en: And then in the fall and winter, it came roaring back.
sentences.zh: 然后在秋季和冬季，它又猛烈地卷土重来。

sentences.en: And a third of the deaths took place in a little tiny period between September and December 1918.
sentences.zh: 三分之一的死亡人数发生在1918年9月到12月之间那短短的一段时间里。

sentences.en: So I'm very worried that something like that could happen this fall and winter, and that we're not mentally prepared for it.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常担心今年秋冬可能会发生类似的事情，而我们在心理上还没有做好准备。

sentences.en: So the infection and death rate for the next few months, quite likely will not be representative of what this virus is capable of.
sentences.zh: 因此，未来几个月的感染率和死亡率很可能无法代表这种病毒的真实威力。

sentences.en: And the fall and the winter may be very, very different and much scarier.
sentences.zh: 而秋季和冬季的情况可能会非常、非常不同，也更可怕。

sentences.en: That's possible.
sentences.zh: 这是有可能的。

sentences.en: And that's what a lot of top public health people are worried about, that we will have transmission.
sentences.zh: 这也是许多顶级公共卫生专家所担心的，即我们将面临持续的传播。

sentences.en: I mean, we're still seeing 20,000 new infections per day.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们每天仍然看到2万例新增感染。

sentences.en: And we're at about a little under 1,000 new deaths per day.
sentences.zh: 而且我们每天的新增死亡人数略低于1000人。

sentences.en: And that's been consistent for a couple of months now.
sentences.zh: 这种情况已经持续了几个月了。

sentences.en: And this might be a strange question, but is that a good number or a bad number?
sentences.zh: 这可能是一个奇怪的问题，但这算是一个好数字还是坏数字？

sentences.en: That's a terrible number.
sentences.zh: 这是一个糟糕透顶的数字。

sentences.en: I mean, 1,000 deaths a day from this?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，每天因这种病毒死亡1000人？

sentences.en: 20,000 new infections a day?
sentences.zh: 每天2万例新增感染？

sentences.en: I mean, that's not an epidemic you have under control.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这不是一场处于控制之下的流行病。

sentences.en: You know, we don't talk about it that way, but that's a rapidly spreading epidemic.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们虽然不这么说，但这确实是一场迅速蔓延的流行病。

sentences.en: Now, we may become complacent about that.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们可能会对此变得自满。

sentences.en: We may sort of accept that as the new norm.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会在某种程度上接受它作为新常态。

sentences.en: And that may lull us into a sense of complacency when fall arrives.
sentences.zh: 这可能会让我们在秋天到来时陷入一种自满的情绪中。

sentences.en: And
sentences.zh: 而

sentences.en: that's a worry.
sentences.zh: 这令人担忧。

sentences.en: And that's why I'm so eager for, you know, treatment or vaccine to hurry up, hurry up, hurry up.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我如此渴望，你知道，治疗方法或疫苗能快点、快点、再快点出来。

sentences.en: And where are we in that vaccine process now?
sentences.zh: 那么我们现在的疫苗研发进展如何？

sentences.en: Uh, well, there's 150 or so vaccine candidates being looked at around the world.
sentences.zh: 嗯，全世界大约有150种疫苗候选方案正在接受评估。

sentences.en: In the United
sentences.zh: 在美国，

sentences.en: States, we have designated different candidates for warp speed, meaning testing the vaccines,
sentences.zh: 我们为“曲速行动”指定了不同的候选疫苗，这意味着在测试疫苗的同时，

sentences.en: but simultaneously paying companies to build factories to make them so that all the ones
sentences.zh: 还要花钱让公司建造工厂来生产它们，这样所有那些

sentences.en: that turn out to be both safe and effective will have hopefully millions of doses ready to roll immediately.
sentences.zh: 被证明既安全又有效的疫苗，有望立即准备好数百万剂供使用。

sentences.en: Because one of the big roadblocks to getting vaccine is not just testing the vaccine
sentences.zh: 因为获得疫苗的一大障碍不仅是测试疫苗

sentences.en: and make sure it works, but then suddenly producing 300 million to 600 million doses for this country,
sentences.zh: 并确保它有效，而是随后突然为这个国家生产3亿到6亿剂疫苗，

sentences.en: depending on if you need one or two doses, and seven plus billion doses for the world.
sentences.zh: 取决于你需要一剂还是两剂，以及为全世界生产70多亿剂。

sentences.en: So you want to get a head start on the production as much as you can.
sentences.zh: 所以你希望尽可能提前开始生产。

sentences.en: And so we're doing that with a number of candidates.
sentences.zh: 我们正在对多个候选疫苗这样做。

sentences.en: And we've never seen anything like this before.
sentences.zh: 我们以前从未见过这样的情况。

sentences.en: Does all that encourage you to think that we might have a vaccine much faster than we've ever had a vaccine before?
sentences.zh: 这一切是否让你认为我们可能会比以往任何时候都更快地获得疫苗？

sentences.en: I remember you telling me that the fastest we've ever really had a vaccine in production and available to people from start to finish is close to four years.
sentences.zh: 我记得你告诉过我，我们从开始到结束真正投入生产并提供给人们的疫苗，最快也要接近四年。

sentences.en: Yes, that was the month's vaccine.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是腮腺炎疫苗。

sentences.en: And the record is four years.
sentences.zh: 纪录是四年。

sentences.en: But I think we're doing things very, very differently this time.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这次我们做事的方式非常、非常不同。

sentences.en: We've got, you know, multiple candidates.
sentences.zh: 我们有，你知道，多个候选方案。

sentences.en: And some of those vaccines, if what we're being told is correct, are actually going into production even as we speak.
sentences.zh: 如果我们要听到的消息属实，其中一些疫苗甚至在我们说话的时候就已经投入生产了。

sentences.en: So that's very encouraging to me.
sentences.zh: 所以这对我来说非常令人鼓舞。

sentences.en: But things go wrong when you test vaccines.
sentences.zh: 但测试疫苗时事情可能会出错。

sentences.en: You get surprises you didn't expect.
sentences.zh: 你会遇到意想不到的惊喜。

sentences.en: And so let's hope multiple things don't go wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们祈祷不要出什么乱子。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《纽约时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Don, we have talked about the risk of many different activities in this moment of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 那么，唐，我们已经讨论过在大流行的这一时刻，许多不同活动的风险。

sentences.en: We have not talked about something that has been going on for several weeks now in the United States,
sentences.zh: 我们还没有讨论在美国已经持续了几周的事情，

sentences.en: which are large-scale protests and demonstrations since the police killing of George Floyd.
sentences.zh: 即自乔治·弗洛伊德被警察杀害以来的大规模抗议和示威活动。

sentences.en: And I wonder what your sense is about the risk involved in those protests of spreading the virus.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你对这些抗议活动中传播病毒的风险有什么看法。

sentences.en: Well, I don't worry when there are crowds outdoors spaced six feet apart and wearing masks.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当人们在户外聚集，保持六英尺距离并戴着口罩时，我不担心。

sentences.en: I do worry when people are jammed up against each other, either confronting a police line or on a dais while they're making speeches or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我担心的是人们挤在一起的时候，无论是面对警察防线，还是在演讲台上发表演讲，或者类似的情况。

sentences.en: I worry about anybody who's pushed into the back of a police van.
sentences.zh: 我担心任何被推入警车后座的人。

sentences.en: I worry about people who've been in cells together.
sentences.zh: 我担心那些被关在一起的人。

sentences.en: I worry about the funeral ceremonies, which all took place indoors.
sentences.zh: 我担心葬礼仪式，它们都是在室内举行的。

sentences.en: You know, these are all potential super spreader situations.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些都是潜在的超级传播情况。

sentences.en: And have we yet seen any uptick in transmission from the U.S.?
sentences.zh: 我们是否已经看到美国出现了传播增加的情况？

sentences.en: I know it may take several weeks for us to determine that, but have we?
sentences.zh: 我知道我们可能需要几周时间才能确定这一点，但我们看到了吗？

sentences.en: I mean, if we have spikes here, it's going to be very hard to say, oh, that spike came from the
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果这里出现了激增，很难说，哦，那个激增来自

sentences.en: proteSt. Because, you know, how do you do contact tracing and everybody else who was in a crowd of
sentences.zh: 抗议活动。因为，你知道，你怎么能对和你一起在1万人的群体中的每个人进行接触者追踪呢？

sentences.en: 10,000 people with you?
sentences.zh: 1万人的群体中。

sentences.en: You know, it's easy to do contact tracing on your family and your co-workers at the office.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对你的家人和办公室的同事进行接触者追踪很容易。

sentences.en: It's very hard to do contact tracing on a whole crowd of strangers.
sentences.zh: 要对一大群陌生人进行接触者追踪是非常困难的。

sentences.en: So we won't necessarily know when people fall ill that they got infected at the protest march.
sentences.zh: 所以当人们生病时，我们不一定知道他们是在抗议游行中被感染的。

sentences.en: I mean, each individual person may say, well, the only time I've been in association with a lot of other people is when I was at the protest march.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，每个人可能会说，嗯，我唯一一次与许多其他人接触是在我参加抗议游行的时候。

sentences.en: But for some epidemiologists to put all those stories together as those people turn up in hospitals or as their grandmothers turn up in hospitals is going to be very difficult.
sentences.zh: 但对于一些流行病学家来说，当这些人出现在医院或他们的祖母出现在医院时，要把所有这些故事拼凑起来将是非常困难的。

sentences.en: So we may not see the signal we would expect to see, if that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可能看不到我们预期的信号，如果这说得通的话。

sentences.en: I'm curious, you know, reflecting on everything that you have just told us, I'm curious how you
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，你知道，回想你刚才告诉我们的一切，我很好奇你

sentences.en: are operating now in the world, knowing everything you now know six months into this pandemic, what your routines are, what your precautions are.
sentences.zh: 现在是如何在这个世界上运作的，了解了你在这场大流行六个月后所知道的一切，你的日常习惯是什么，你的预防措施是什么。

sentences.en: I mean, are you taking the subway?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你在坐地铁吗？

sentences.en: Are you always wearing a mask?
sentences.zh: 你一直戴着口罩吗？

sentences.en: Are you going to any kind of office?
sentences.zh: 你去任何办公室吗？

sentences.en: I'm working from home.
sentences.zh: 我在家工作。

sentences.en: I'm working a lot.
sentences.zh: 我工作很忙。

sentences.en: I'm lucky in that I'm not out of work.
sentences.zh: 我很幸运，我没有失业。

sentences.en: But my girlfriend and a lot of other people I know who are out of work are pent up and frustrated and angry and some are really worried about their income.
sentences.zh: 但我女朋友和我认识的许多其他失业的人感到压抑、沮丧和愤怒，有些人真的很担心他们的收入。

sentences.en: I always wear a mask when I am indoors with other people, as in the grocery store or pharmacy.
sentences.zh: 当我和其他人一起在室内时，比如在杂货店或药店，我总是戴着口罩。

sentences.en: I avoid going indoors with other people basically at all costs.
sentences.zh: 我基本上不惜一切代价避免与其他人一起进入室内。

sentences.en: If I were riding the subway, I would definitely wear a mask.
sentences.zh: 如果我要坐地铁，我肯定会戴口罩。

sentences.en: I'm not riding the subway.
sentences.zh: 我没有坐地铁。

sentences.en: I'm very worried about what's going to happen in New York City when a lot of people have to go back to work.
sentences.zh: 我非常担心当很多人不得不回去工作时，纽约市会发生什么。

sentences.en: Because, you know, right now we've got near gridlock on the FDR drive and stuff sometimes because a lot more people are in cars because they're afraid to go into the subway.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，现在FDR大道等地有时几乎陷入瘫痪，因为更多的人在开车，因为他们害怕进入地铁。

sentences.en: But at some point, we're going to have to go back into the subway.
sentences.zh: 但在某个时候，我们将不得不回到地铁里。

sentences.en: And frankly,
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，

sentences.en: I think the MTA ought to take the windows off the buses and subways.
sentences.zh: 我认为大都会运输署（MTA）应该把公共汽车和地铁的窗户拆掉。

sentences.en: I know it's crazy, but and I know it's going to be cold in winter and hot and air conditioned in summer.
sentences.zh: 我知道这很疯狂，而且我知道冬天会很冷，夏天会有空调，但

sentences.en: But that's the way to get breeze blowing through and closed spaces.
sentences.zh: 那是让微风吹过封闭空间的方法。

sentences.en: And if we want to go back into our offices, we're going to have to find a way to have breeze blowing through and closed spaces so that the virus does not hang in the air.
sentences.zh: 如果我们想回到办公室，我们将不得不找到一种方法让微风吹过封闭空间，这样病毒就不会悬浮在空气中。

sentences.en: We're going to have to rethink our workplaces or stay out of them because they're going to be too dangerous until we have a vaccine.
sentences.zh: 我们将不得不重新思考我们的工作场所，否则就不要去那里，因为在我们有疫苗之前，它们会太危险。

sentences.en: Do you intend to return to an office anytime soon?
sentences.zh: 你打算很快回到办公室吗？

sentences.en: No, I'm 66 years old.
sentences.zh: 不，我66岁了。

sentences.en: I'm in a, you know, I'm reasonably healthy, but I'm also in a higher risk group.
sentences.zh: 我处于，你知道，我身体还算健康，但我也属于高风险群体。

sentences.en: So I think me being in an office with a lot of members of the daily team breathing on the microphones or whatever would be dangerous for me right now.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我现在和许多每日团队成员一起在办公室里对着麦克风呼吸或其他什么，对我来说会很危险。

sentences.en: So, no, and I'm sad that I, you know, I have not seen my granddaughter except on video.
sentences.zh: 所以，不，我很伤心，你知道，我除了在视频里，还没有见过我的孙女。

sentences.en: She was born on the 4th.
sentences.zh: 她是在4号出生的。

sentences.en: And, um, thank you.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: And, you know, and, and I intend not to hold her until I'm vaccinated or immune, you know, my daughter, the apple did not fall far from the tree.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我打算在接种疫苗或产生免疫力之前不抱她，你知道，我女儿，苹果没有掉在离树很远的地方。

sentences.en: And she's just as determined as I am that we should play by the rules on that, I think.
sentences.zh: 她和我一样坚定，我认为我们应该遵守规则。

sentences.en: So, um, you know, it's sad, but it's, um, I'm taking the long view.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，你知道，这很令人难过，但我，嗯，我看得比较长远。

sentences.en: This increases the chances that both Darrow, that's her name, Darrow Maeve McNeil Kaye, and I will make it to her high school graduation.
sentences.zh: 这增加了达罗（Darrow），那是她的名字，达罗·梅芙·麦克尼尔·凯（Darrow Maeve McNeil Kaye），和我能参加她高中毕业典礼的机会。

sentences.en: So that's the plan.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是计划。

sentences.en: And if I have to sacrifice a little bit of seeing her right now, um, you know, okay, I'll make that sacrifice for both of us.
sentences.zh: 如果我现在不得不牺牲一点见她的机会，嗯，你知道，好吧，我会为我们俩做出那个牺牲。

sentences.en: Well, we wish both of you the best and we're really grateful for your time.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们祝愿你们俩一切顺利，我们真的很感谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: And thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you for letting me on again.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你再次邀请我。

sentences.en: The Times reports that as infections rise in 22 American states, officials there are facing a
sentences.zh: 《时报》报道称，随着美国22个州的感染人数上升，那里的官员正面临一个

sentences.en: choice, accept the increase as the cost of reopening their economies or slow the reopening process and even impose new restrictions, however unpopular they may be.
sentences.zh: 选择：接受这种增长作为重启经济的代价，或者放慢重启进程，甚至实施新的限制措施，无论它们多么不受欢迎。

sentences.en: In an interview published on Sunday,
sentences.zh: 在周日发表的一次采访中，

sentences.en: Dr. Anthony Fauci, a White House advisor on the pandemic, said that waves of infections would likely spike and fall for months and that he did not expect the U.S.
sentences.zh: 白宫大流行顾问安东尼·福奇博士表示，感染浪潮可能会在几个月内反复起伏，他预计美国

sentences.en: to return to normal for another year.
sentences.zh: 在一年内无法恢复正常。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know day.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: The chief of police in Atlanta resigned over the weekend after an officer she oversees killed a 27-year-old Black man,
sentences.zh: 亚特兰大警察局长在周末辞职，此前她监管的一名警官杀害了一名27岁的黑人男子，

sentences.en: Rayshard Brooks.
sentences.zh: 雷沙德·布鲁克斯（Rayshard Brooks）。

sentences.en: Before he was shot to death, Brooks had failed a sobriety test, run from the police and grabbed a taser from an arresting officer.
sentences.zh: 在被枪杀之前，布鲁克斯未能通过清醒测试，从警察手中逃跑，并从一名逮捕他的警官手中抢走了一把泰瑟枪。

sentences.en: A sequence of events that Atlanta's mayor,
sentences.zh: 这一系列事件，亚特兰大市长，

sentences.en: Keisha Lance Bottoms, said did not warrant his death.
sentences.zh: 凯莎·兰斯·博顿斯（Keisha Lance Bottoms）表示，并不足以导致他的死亡。

sentences.en: While there may be debate as to whether this was an appropriate use of deadly force,
sentences.zh: 虽然对于这是否是适当使用致命武力可能存在争论，

sentences.en: I firmly believe that there is a clear distinction between what you can do and what you should do.
sentences.zh: 但我坚信，你能做什么和你应该做什么之间有明显的区别。

sentences.en: I do not believe that this was a justified use of deadly force.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这是正当使用致命武力。

sentences.en: Bottoms immediately ordered that the officer who had killed Brooks be fired.
sentences.zh: 博顿斯立即下令解雇了那名杀害布鲁克斯的警官。

sentences.en: And the Times reports that protests over the death of George Floyd have been held in more than
sentences.zh: 据《纽约时报》报道，针对乔治·弗洛伊德之死的抗议活动已在
全美2000多个

sentences.en: cities and towns across all 50 states over the past three weeks.
sentences.zh: 城镇举行，遍布所有50个州，持续了过去三周。

sentences.en: The protests, the Times found, defied traditional demographic fault lines, occurring not just in Democratic strongholds, but in rural, conservative, and majority-white communities.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》发现，这些抗议活动打破了传统的人口统计学界限，不仅发生在民主党的大本营，也出现在乡村、保守派地区以及以白人为主的社区。

sentences.en: The protests continued over the weekend, from Brooklyn to the small town of
sentences.zh: 抗议活动在周末持续进行，从布鲁克林一直到

sentences.en: Haughton, Louisiana.
sentences.zh: 路易斯安那州霍顿这样的小镇。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目，我们将为您准备假日待客指南。

sentences.zh: 敬请收听，获取让客人们宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们需要全黑环境才能入睡吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they black out to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是喝醉了才睡着。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这可是个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏或食物不耐受的情况吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？
